newsitem.title: USA: Clinton fund-raiser denies working for China,Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Clinton fund-raiser denies working for China,Taiwan.

text.p: A friend of President Bill Clinton who fled to Asia last autumn after questions arose about his part in illegal campaign contributions denied on Tuesday he was working for China or Taiwan.

Charles Yah Lin Trie declined to talk to NBC Nightly News anchor Tom Brokaw on camera, but Brokaw said Trie vehemently denied working for either Asian country and said he never received even one dollar from either government.
The network showed footage of Trie and Brokaw walking together in Shanghai, China. Trie told NBC that friends in China have been hiding him, but that he did nothing wrong.

Trie, a one-time restaurant owner in the president's home town of Little Rock, Arkansas, became an international consultant and helped raise $1.2 million for the Clintons' legal defense fund. The funds have since been returned because the source of them could not be identified, NBC reported.

The Justice Department and several congressional committees are investigating fund-raising activities and Republicans have urged Attorney General Janet Reno to appoint an independent counsel to delve deeper.

Trie, who made a million dollars as a consultant in 1993, told NBC he is now broke and his business dried up after reports of campaign finance irregularities, and his alleged involvement, began to emerge in news reports.

Trie said he knew Wang Jun, the suspected arms dealer whom he had invited to a White House coffee meeting with Clinton in February 1996, solely as a powerful businessman and not as a weapons dealer, NBC said.
Clinton later said it was inappropriate that Wang was allowed in the White House. His company was implicated in an alleged scheme to smuggle guns into the United States.

In the NBC interview, Trie described former DNC fund-raiser and Commerce Department official John Huang, another central figure in the fund-raising scandal, as a friend, but said he knew nothing of possible Huang ties to China.

Trie said he raised money for Clinton's defense fund but acted only as a courier for the Buddhist community, many of whose checks were returned because the donors were barely literate immigrants with no addresses or phone numbers on the checks.

Trie said he never spoke with Clinton about political issues, although he did write a letter to the president last year urging him not to send a U.S. aircraft carrier to the Taiwan Straits because of tensions between China and Taiwan. He thought the action would hurt Clinton and it would also be bad for Trie's business as a trade consultant.
